title: A は B より ～ : More Than

blocks.content: **より** marks the baseline of comparison : what you are comparing *against*. What comes before より is the lesser item; what comes before the adjective is the greater one.

lines: A は B **より** [adjective] です       ← A is more ~ than B
B **より** A **のほうが** [adjective] です  ← A is more ~ than B (emphatic)

rows.japanese: 東京は大阪より大きいです。
rows.romaji: Tōkyō wa Ōsaka yori ōkii desu.

rows.japanese: バスより電車のほうが速いです。
rows.romaji: Basu yori densha no hō ga hayai desu.
rows.english: The train is faster than the bus.

rows.japanese: 夏より冬のほうが好きです。
rows.romaji: Natsu yori fuyu no hō ga suki desu.

rows.japanese: 昨日より今日のほうが寒いです。
rows.romaji: Kinō yori kyō no hō ga samui desu.

rows.japanese: 肉より魚のほうが好きです。
rows.romaji: Niku yori sakana no hō ga suki desu.
rows.english: I like fish more than meat.

blocks.content: Adding のほうが after the item being elevated makes the comparison more explicit and emphatic. Both structures are grammatically correct : のほうが is simply more common in natural speech.
